text: 🇲🇽✊ "With great honor, I am a housewife, I am a mother, I am a grandmother and, by the will of the people of Mexico, Supreme Commander of the Armed Forces." — Presidenta Claudia Sheinbaum, Honesty and Results, Villahermosa, Tabasco Her answer to a comedian who said, when she took office, that "a housewife has reached the presidency." "Nobody should mock a housewife. Nobody," she said. "We women can be whatever we want to be. There are no limits." Women aged 60 to 64 receive the Pensión Mujeres Bienestar in recognition of the care work they have always done.

🇲🇽🌎 "The cravings of foreign powers have always been on our territory." "That's why we must never forget that sovereignty resides in the people… And whoever distances themselves from the people also distances themselves from the homeland." — Presidenta Claudia Sheinbaum, Honesty and Results, Villahermosa, Tabasco She recalled that after Madero won the presidency, a US ambassador in Mexico promoted the coup against him; Victoriano Huerta took power and Madero was murdered. In 1914 the United States again positioned itself off Veracruz trying to invade, and the revolutionaries did not allow it. During the French intervention, it was the conservatives who went looking for an emperor to govern Mexico.

text: 🇲🇽🏥 Tabasco is getting 463 free doctor's offices, in every single municipality. "Sometimes you get sick and either you go to a private doctor who charges you, or to the pharmacy doctors, and then you have to buy the medicine, or you go straight to the health center or the hospital, and what you have isn't necessarily serious… So we decided to build first-contact health care." — Presidenta Claudia Sheinbaum, Honesty and Results, Villahermosa, Tabasco Each office will have a small pharmacy with the most important medicines. They are built this year and open next year, totally free. The 93-bed Cárdenas hospital, abandoned for years, is about to open, and a new 260-bed IMSS hospital in Villahermosa will serve the whole population. Tabasco receives 20,610 million pesos a year in well-being programs, plus nearly 30,000 million in infrastructure.

🇲🇽✊ "We women love our husbands, our family, but we have the right and the duty to fight for our homeland too." — Presidenta Claudia Sheinbaum quoting Leona Vicario, Honesty and Results, Villahermosa, Tabasco Leona Vicario, a wealthy woman, gave all her money to the independence fighters and was Mexico's first woman journalist, Sheinbaum recalled. When the conservative Lucas Alamán wrote that she had joined independence only because she was Andrés Quintana Roo's wife, she answered him with that letter. At this year's Grito, Sheinbaum named four women of independence, calling Josefa Ortiz by her own surnames, Téllez Girón, "not as the wife of."

🇲🇽🛢️ <u>IF TRUMP BANS DIESEL EXPORTS, MEXICO HAS 13 DAYS</u>

Mexico burns about 400,000 barrels of diesel a day and imports 30–50% of it. With no strategic fuel stockpile, Pemex and private storage cover roughly 13 days of demand if Washington goes ahead with a 90-day export ban, El Financiero reports. Pemex owns Deer Park in Houston — but the refinery answers to US law, not Mexico's.

🔥🇲🇽 <u>THE "1,600 BABY TEETH" GRAVE NO ONE CAN FIND</u>

Michoacán's State Prosecutor says it has "no knowledge nor any record" of an intervention involving a clandestine grave with 1,600 children's teeth in Zacapu — and federal prosecutors have none either. No complaint or forensic request of that kind has been logged since 2021. The claim, launched in a Milenio column, was amplified by PRI chief Alejandro Moreno and a lineup of opposition commentators before anyone checked.

🇲🇽🌎 <u>SHEINBAUM: FIVE VETOES SHOULDN'T RUN THE WORLD</u>

President Sheinbaum called for strengthening and reforming the United Nations so it can actually address conflicts like Palestine, questioning that its key decisions stay concentrated in the five permanent Security Council members — the US, China, Russia, France and the UK — each holding a veto. Mexico's compass stays the same: peaceful settlement of disputes, self-determination of peoples, multilateralism. On Bachelet's failed bid for Secretary-General, settled among the veto powers: "a profound reform of the international organization would be very good."
banner: UN: SHEINBAUM CALLS FOR DEEP REFORM

text:
🔥🇲🇽 <u>47 OFFICIALS AND ONE COMPANY SANCTIONED IN MEXICO'S ANTI-CORRUPTION SWEEP</u>

Mexico's Anti-Corruption and Good Governance Secretariat sanctioned 47 public servants and one company — dismissals, bans of up to 10 years and 4.6 million pesos in fines. Among them: a CFE worker in Puebla banned for 10 years over nine fake medical certificates; an official at the Durango military hospital fined 651,000 pesos for supply and gas payments he couldn't account for; and a company fined 3.1 million pesos and barred for four years for submitting altered vehicle invoices in a public tender.

🇲🇽🇵🇸 <u>MEXICO JOINS THE HAGUE GROUP TO DEFEND INTERNATIONAL COURTS AND PALESTINE</u>

At UN headquarters, Mexico sat with some 40 nations convened by South Africa and Malaysia to defend the International Criminal Court, the International Court of Justice and the Palestinian people — after days of attacks and threats against those courts from Washington, Israel and their right-wing allies. Mexico, Brazil, Cuba and Norway joined the Hague Group. Mexico's alternate UN representative, Porfirio Thierry Muñoz Ledo: "We have to ensure and improve compliance and implementation of international law."
banner: HAGUE GROUP: MEXICO DEFENDS THE COURTS

🇲🇽🤝 <u>1.6 MILLION PEOPLE IN GUERRERO NOW RECEIVE WELFARE PROGRAMS</u>

In Acapulco — battered by two hurricanes in 2023 and 2024 — President Sheinbaum reported that federal Bienestar programs now reach 1,637,427 people in Guerrero, alongside road, health, education and urban works across the state. "Education is the best vaccine against insecurity and crime," she said. "Nothing above those who have the least, nothing above the people — Guerrero will always be with the transformation."
